subject: First steps in NIMBLE with capture-recapture data. How include an interaction term?

messages.author: 18fd6ba17c8f2827
messages.subject: First steps in NIMBLE with capture-recapture data. How include an interaction term?
parts:
Hi everyone!

I am new to Nimble! I attended a fabolous workshop on Bayesian analysis of capture recapture data by Olivier Gimenez, Chloe Nater, Sarah Cubaynes, Maud Quéroué and Perry de Valpine.

I am currently learning how to specify multievent models in Nimble and while the most simple "types" of models (phi, psi and p as constants and with a group covariate  (sex)), I am having a lot of 'trouble' in including an interaction term between a grouping covariate and time. It is here where I am getting aware of the difference between working with 'black-box' programs and having to specify yourself everything! (Very insightful!)

I am using the dipper dataset and the results provided by MARK as a guide to know if I am doing things correctly, but I can't find the way. So, it is very likely that I am not specifying the interaction in the proper way.

This is the code that I wrote (modified from those provided at the workshop for the survival live demo).


## Libraries
library(nimble)
library(tidyverse)
library(MCMCvis)

## Data
dipper <- read_csv("dipper.csv")
sex <- if_else(dipper$sex == "M", 0, 1)
sex

## Formatting the data
y <- dipper %>%
  select(year_1981:year_1987) %>%
  as.matrix()
head(y)

## Model specificiation
hmm.phip <- nimbleCode({
  p ~ dunif(0, 1) # prior detection
  for(i in 1:N){
    for(t in 1:(T-1)){
      logit(phi[i,t]) <- beta[1] + beta[2]*sex[i] + lambda[t] + iota[t]*sex[i]
      gamma[1,1,i,t] <- phi[i,t]      # Pr(alive t -> alive t+1)
      gamma[1,2,i,t] <- 1 - phi[i,t]  # Pr(alive t -> dead t+1)
      gamma[2,1,i,t] <- 0        # Pr(dead t -> alive t+1)
      gamma[2,2,i,t] <- 1
    } #time
  } # sex
  for(t in 1:(T-1)){
    lambda[t] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = 1.5)
    iota[t]  ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = 1.5)
    phi_male[t] <- 1/((1+exp(-beta[1]+lambda[t]))) # phi[t] males
    phi_female[t] <- 1/((1+exp(-beta[1]+beta[2]+lambda[t]+iota[t]))) # phi[t] females
  }
  beta[1] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = 1.5)
  beta[2] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = 1.5)
  # Pr(dead t -> dead t+1)
  delta[1] <- 1          # Pr(alive t = 1) = 1
  delta[2] <- 0          # Pr(dead t = 1) = 0
  omega[1,1] <- 1 - p    # Pr(alive t -> non-detected t)
  omega[1,2] <- p        # Pr(alive t -> detected t)
  omega[2,1] <- 1        # Pr(dead t -> non-detected t)
  omega[2,2] <- 0        # Pr(dead t -> detected t)
  # likelihood
  for (i in 1:N){
    z[i,first[i]] ~ dcat(delta[1:2])
    for (j in (first[i]+1):T){
      z[i,j] ~ dcat(gamma[z[i,j-1], 1:2, i, j-1])
      y[i,j] ~ dcat(omega[z[i,j], 1:2])
    }
  }
})

## Get the occasion of first capture for all individuals.
first <- apply(y, 1, function(x) min(which(x !=0)))

## A list with constants.
my.constants <- list(N = nrow(y),
                     T = ncol(y),
                     first = first,
                     sex=sex)


## Now the data in a list. Note that we add 1 to the data to have 1 for non-detections and 2 for detections.
my.data <- list(y = y + 1)

## Specify initial values. For the latent states, we go for the easy way, and say that all individuals are alive through the study period.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
zinits <- y + 1 # non-detection -> alive
zinits[zinits == 2] <- 1 # dead -> alive

initial.values <- function() list(beta = runif(2,0,1),
                                  lambda = runif(my.constants$T-1, 0,1),
                                  iota = runif(my.constants$T-1, 0, 1),
                                  p = runif(1,0,1),
                                  z = zinits)
initial.values()

## Specify the parameters we wish to monitor.
parameters.to.save <- c("beta", "lambda", "iota", "phi_male", "phi_female", "p")

## MCMC details.
n.iter <- 50000
n.burnin <- 5000
n.chains <- 2

## At last, let's run nimble.
mcmc.phip <- nimbleMCMC(code = hmm.phip,
                        constants = my.constants,
                        data = my.data,              
                        inits = initial.values,
                        monitors = parameters.to.save,
                        niter = n.iter,
                        nburnin = n.burnin,
                        nchains = n.chains)

 
## Examine the results.
MCMCsummary(mcmc.phip, round = 2)
MCMCtrace(object = mcmc.phip,pdf = FALSE)


Thank you and sorry for asking such a naive question.

Iraida
